problem: Traditional VLN methods struggle with cross-modal alignment, generalization and real-time decision-making, and LLM-generated commands often mismatch the agent's predefined executable command set.
motivation: Reliable natural-language navigation needs LLM planning outputs to map onto commands the agent can actually execute, especially in dynamic environments. Command mismatch between free-form LLM output and predefined actions hurts success rates and efficiency.
key_idea: Use an LLM as the planner, then vectorise both predefined and LLM-generated commands and use k-nearest neighbours to select the best-matching executable command, resolving ambiguity/mismatch.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract suggests that embedding-space matching (kNN) between generated and predefined commands is what bridges free-form LLM output and executable actions.
method: LLM planner: an LLM converts natural language instructions into navigation plans/commands.
Command vectorisation: predefined commands and LLM-generated commands are both embedded as vectors.
kNN matching: k-nearest neighbours finds the optimal predefined command for each generated command, resolving mismatches.
